overall: The AG found the Sewer Commission violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating by email on May 8 when a member's opinions on noticed topics reached a quorum; the May 4 allegation was declined because it was not raised with the commission first.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged that on May 8 a commission member's emailed opinions on noticed topics, shared with a quorum, was deliberation outside a posted meeting.
allegations.key_passage: We agree and conclude that the May 8 email sent by Mr. Luck violated the Open Meeting Law because it constituted a communication that reached a quorum of the public body.

allegations.summary: Complaint also alleged email deliberation on May 4, which was not included in the complaint filed with the commission.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation because it was not included in a complaint to the Commission and the Commission has not had an opportunity to respond to it.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the law’s requirements, and we caution that similar future violations could be considered evidence of intent to violate the law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
